question: If every reading is repeated r times and majority-voted before the solver sees it, does the residual flip count fall low enough that the least noise budget is found inside the 10 s query cap, so that active identification works on noisy traces, and what do the extra reads cost?
motivation: Study 035 (Observed): on all 24 noisy cases A10's B = 0 search was UNSAT and the upward least-B search (B = 1, 2, ...) hit the 10 s cap after 9-12 queries, below the true flip count (13-23 in 177 readings), so B stayed 0 and A10 stopped IDU. A10_fixed (B = 27 from the start) was IDU on every case, clean included. Inferred: the UNSAT proofs just below the least B are the hard queries, and their hardness grows with B. At eps 0.05 a 3-read majority flips with probability 3e^2-2e^3 = 0.00725 (about 1.3 expected flips in 177 readings) and a 5-read majority with probability 0.00116 (about 0.2) (Exact arithmetic; Inferred effect)

hypotheses.H1_repeat: A11_r3 (A10 on a majority-of-3 trace, least B by bisection) identifies noisy 12-state machines: ID(A11_r3) - ID(A10) >= +0.25 at noisy12 with WRONG 0 within budget
hypotheses.H2_r_vs_budget: more repeats lower the final B and the capped-query count monotonically (r = 1, 3, 5), at a read cost linear in r
hypotheses.H3_no_clean_cost: on clean traces the majority equals the single reading, so A11_r3 labels equal A9 labels on every clean case and its final B is 0
hypotheses.H4_cap: arming the host timer at 9.5 s keeps every query of every arm, S7 included, under 10.5 s

arms.A11_r3: new file brute/scalesearch11.py: A10 logic with two changes. (1) Every reading, on the base trace and on every executed separating word, is taken r = 3 times at the same position (the world wrapper re-reads the current output without stepping) and the majority is the reading the solver sees; the solver never sees the raw reads. (2) The least B is found by bisection over [0, B_max(r)] (first B = 0, then B_max(r), then midpoints), not by the upward chain; B never falls and is re-bisected only on a new contradiction. B_max(r) = the declared-rate B_end rule applied to the majority flip rate. Stop rule, K and the rival searches as A10
arms.A11_r3_up: ablation: A11_r3 with A10's upward least-B search instead of bisection; separates the effect of repeats from the effect of the search order
arms.A10: frozen v0.32.0 arm (brute/scalesearch10), r = 1, unchanged (control; its 035 behaviour is the prediction)
arms.S7: passive noisy v0.29.0 arm with the identify probe, unchanged; reported and in GQB11
arms.S5: passive clean v0.27.0 arm, unchanged; gated only on clean cases and controls (declared before data, because 035 showed it answers WRONG on noisy traces by design); its noisy labels are reported

design.query_cap: as 035 (host-side threading.Timer calling the solver's interrupt; brute/ stays host-agnostic), but the timer is armed at 9.5 s instead of 10 s for every arm, to absorb the interrupt latency that let S7 reach 10.538 s in 035. An interrupted query counts as unknown (IDU path)
design.noise: independent reading flips at eps 0.05 on every raw read on noisy cases (repeats are independent draws); eps 0 on clean cases and controls; the declared rate is given to every noise-aware arm
design.cost_accounting: reads (raw world output reads), steps (world actions) and extra actions are reported per arm; a repeated read costs one read and no step
design.world_access: step-and-reread wrapper over experiments/worlds_026.py; the truth is used only by the scorer
design.labels: as 035: ID, IDF, AMB, WRONG, IDU. A noisy case is 'within budget' for an arm if the true flip count of the trace that arm's solver sees is <= its B_max at every step; WRONG is gated on within-budget cases and reported on the rest
design.budget: 120 s per arm per case; 9.5 s timer, 10.5 s bound per SAT query; K = 64
